One-line judgment: coating, painting, and spraying machine setters, operators, and tenders are not 'just spraying a few strokes with a gun'; they set up, operate, or tend spraying and roll-coating machines that apply coatings or paint to products such as glassware, fabric, ceramics, metal, plastic, paper, or wood, using varnish, silver paste, copper, rubber, clear oil, glaze, enamel, oils, or rust-preventive materials. O*NET defines this occupation as 'setting up, operating, or tending spraying or roll-coating machines that apply coatings or paint to products such as glassware, fabric, ceramics, metal, plastic, paper, or wood, and includes transportation equipment painters such as painters in automotive body repair shops', and this page follows the exact occupation of O*NET-SOC 51-9124.00; under the official basis, the Chinese title corresponding to frozen number 0178 is this occupation, and this page explains its substantive duties using the official definition.

Signals to keep exploring: you are willing to repeat work to the line beat beside a coating line or coating station over the long term, while keeping an eye on viscosity, air pressure, gun travel speed, and appearance defects; O*NET work context shows 87% use their hands to handle and feel tools and workpieces continually or almost continually, 70% make repetitive motions continually, 69% stand continually or almost continually, 79% are exposed to distracting or uncomfortable noise every day, 74% are exposed to contaminants every day, 58% are exposed to hazardous conditions every day, 76% wear common protective or safety equipment every day, 68% face strict time limits every day, and 65% hold face-to-face discussions every day.

Conditions for pausing before heavy investment: you have not yet walked through a complete loop of 'machine setup and test spray, applying the coating, inspecting appearance and measuring, stopping the line to handle an anomaly, and cleaning and recording', and have not checked the local and employer requirements for hazardous chemical communication, hazardous energy isolation, machine guarding, and personal protective equipment; the preparation level for this occupation is Job Zone 1-2 (little or some preparation), with an SVP below 6.0, and the education distribution on the page shows 63% of respondents answering that a high school diploma or equivalent is required, 27% answering below a high school diploma, and 7% answering that a postsecondary certificate is required (the page shows only these three tiers); the occupation page does not mark this code as Bright Outlook, and this page does not infer an individual hiring probability from that.

Education, training, certification, and job authorization must each be checked separately: O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone 1-2 (little or some preparation), with an SVP below 6.0, and the education distribution on the page is mainly a high school diploma and below; the page provides 22 national certifications (mostly coating inspection certifications), but certification is not a license, signing authority, or employer authorization; in the United States, the employer's obligations for hazardous chemical communication, hazardous energy control, machine guarding, and personal protective equipment are set by the applicable occupational safety regulations and assessed item by item at each workplace; this page describes tasks and boundaries based on O*NET and public sources, and does not write a degree or certification as a legal qualification.

One-line summary: this is an occupation where whether the film can be laid evenly, whether equipment guarding and hazardous energy hold, and whether chemicals and waste are handled per procedure determines success more than personal hand speed; if you are willing to treat safety and process parameters as hard daily standards, it deserves serious consideration.

The work of coating, painting, and spraying machine setters, operators, and tenders falls into three connected but independent work surfaces. The first is equipment setup and operation control: starting and stopping equipment with levers or buttons, attaching hoses or nozzles with wrenches and pliers and adjusting to the proper spray dispersion, turning knobs and handwheels and valves or switches to regulate conveyor speed, machine temperature, air pressure and circulation, and the flow or spray volume of coating or paint, observing machine gauges and equipment operation to find defects or deviations from standards and adjusting promptly, moving workpieces or products through or around machine rollers and dryers, loading material into hoppers, tanks, vats, or pans for coating or paint or spraying, and weighing or measuring chemicals or coating or paint before adding them to the machine. The second is applying coatings and judging appearance: holding or adjusting the direction of the spray gun to spray coating onto workpieces, spraying primer and decorative or topcoat layers at the specified amounts on prepared surfaces, applying rust-preventive primer and sealing and caulking seams, hand-touching up areas that need repair or that the gun cannot reach with a brush, monitoring the spray operation to identify defects such as blistering or streaks and correcting their causes, judging paint flow and viscosity and coating quality by visual inspection or a viscometer, inspecting and measuring and weighing or testing samples to confirm they meet specifications, and sanding and waxing the finished finish. The third is cleaning and maintenance and material and waste handling: disassembling, cleaning, and reassembling sprayers or power equipment with solvents and wire brushes and cloths, cleaning equipment and the work area, using tools to remove material, parts, or workpieces from spraying or coating equipment, operating auxiliary machines or equipment in the coating or spraying process, operating hoists or conveyors to move equipment or materials to the spray area, setting up portable equipment such as fans, exhausts, ladders, or scaffolding, and disposing of hazardous waste in a proper manner and recording operating data on the prescribed forms. O*NET Updated2026 currently has 29 tasks: 16 core, 7 supplementary, and 6 New with importance Not available, which are not filled in as 0 or 13 supplementary. The first 3 are proper hazardous waste disposal 86, spray guns 85, and specified primer and topcoat 83; the new items added are heating, ventilation, and drying, primer repair, body filler, color matching, surface removal of oil, rust, and old paint, and sanding and sealing dried finish. The heat source and old paint handling among the new tasks are statistical tasks only and do not replace on-site fire prevention and operational authorization.
Set up, operate, or tend spraying and roll-coating machines to apply coating or paint to product surfaces at the specified amounts and process conditions

Verify workpiece and coating → set up the machine and test spray → apply primer and topcoat → inspect appearance and measure samples → clean equipment and dispose of waste → record operating data and hand off
Complete the coating or painting to process requirements and leave reviewable setup and inspection and handling records

Verify workpiece and coating requirements → set parameters and confirm them with a test spray → apply the coating at the specified amounts → identify and correct appearance defects → clean equipment and dispose of hazardous waste → record the batch and parameters and anomalies

Setup and parameter records, test spray and first-article confirmation records, appearance and film thickness and viscosity inspection records, equipment disassembly and cleaning records, chemical requisition and hazardous waste disposal records, operating data records and anomaly and shutdown handling records, and shift handover records.

Adjacent architectural coating can spray and coat equipment structures, and hand finishing can also use a handheld spray gun; automotive repair includes body straightening and parts and glass, and automotive painting is already included in this occupation, so the two are not mutually exclusive. Mechanical repair and maintenance focus on repairing and servicing equipment, and duties may overlap; fiberglass lamination focuses on layup and mold forming, electroplating involves molten metal or electrolytic coatings, and cleaning equipment is not limited to metal pickling. This occupation focuses on setting up, operating, and tending spray and roll-coating machines and on coating inspection.
Apply coating or paint steadily to product surfaces within safety and process constraints and leave reviewable records

Work to the beat in manufacturing workshops and at spray lines or coating stations; hazardous energy isolation and machine guarding and chemical handling follow employer and applicable regulatory requirements
Based on coating specifications, process parameters, equipment gauge readings, viscosity and appearance inspection results, and equipment and safety procedures

Architectural and maintenance painters coat structures such as buildings and bridges and equipment, may use brushes or rollers or spraying, and verify surface materials; this occupation focuses on machine spraying and roll coating for various products and is not simply classified by whether a spray gun is used.
Verify requirements, set up and test spray, apply the coating, inspect appearance and measure, clean and dispose, record and hand off

Hand-finishing occupations may use handheld spray guns and pens and brushes to coat products and inspect them; this occupation focuses on setting up, operating, and tending spray and roll-coating machines, actual tasks overlap, and hand finishing is not limited to brushes and rollers.

Setup parameter records, first-article and test spray records, appearance and film thickness and viscosity inspection records, chemical and hazardous waste records, operating data and anomaly handling records

Industrial machinery repair and mechanical maintenance focus on equipment repair and serviceability and may overlap with cleaning and maintaining coating equipment, so it cannot be asserted that they never apply coatings; repair and isolation follow the specific duty's training and authority.

Personal and equipment safety comes first, and any included internal repair and maintenance is controlled under the hazardous energy procedure first; guards must not be bypassed without authorization to operate equipment in a hazardous condition, chemicals are checked against the SDS label and the hazard assessment, waste identified as hazardous is handed over in lawful categories, and anomalies beyond your authority mean stopping and escalating. U.S. OSHA1910.147 is limited to the repair and maintenance hazardous energy it covers; general production has its applicable conditions and exceptions, and not all setup and cleaning is judged to require LOTO. A person performing isolation must have the authorized employee duties and training under the employer's procedure, and ordinary operator status does not automatically authorize it; stored residual energy must be eliminated, disconnected, restrained, or made safe, with re-accumulation checked continuously where necessary, isolation and de-energization verified before work, and a stop button is not an isolating device. Re-energization follows the procedure for checking that equipment and personnel are clear and for notification, and is not decided by the operator simply because the anomaly has disappeared. U.S. 1910.132 requires the employer to assess hazards and select suitable and properly fitting PPE and provide training; 1910.134 prioritizes feasible engineering controls, requires a medical evaluation before respirator use, and requires fit testing for tight-fitting facepieces on first use and model or size change and at least annually. PPE does not replace ventilation, position authority, or judgment of safe dwell time. The 1910.107 ventilation provisions are limited to the applicable scenarios of spraying combustible or flammable materials. China's current Ecological Environment Code takes effect 2026-08-15; Articles 528–536 identify hazardous waste by list or identification, require identification marks, unit plans and ledgers and reporting, standardized storage, utilization, and disposal, classification by characteristics, and prohibit mixing incompatible materials without safe disposal; dumping or discarding without authorization or mixing into non-hazardous waste storage is prohibited, operating units must hold a permit, and entrusting unlicensed units or individuals is prohibited, with transfers following the manifest and cross-province approval rules. Article 1242 has repealed the old solid waste law, which is no longer used as the current basis.

Editorial process check: check viscosity and air pressure and speed and film thickness against the approved process and the actual material, and for anomalies stop and escalate per the on-site safety and quality procedure, with adjustment and confirmation by authorized personnel, not self-release based on a general paragraph.

paragraphs: The six directions share some capabilities with this occupation: coating and material knowledge, equipment handling feel, appearance judgment experience, and safety and record habits. The real differences lie in the object and the responsibility: architectural and maintenance painters face buildings and structures on site, automotive body and glass repairers face a single vehicle, painters in the hand-finishing direction focus on brush application and decorative effects, industrial machinery mechanics and maintenance workers take the equipment itself as their object without applying coatings, fiberglass laminators and fabricators focus on composite forming, while this occupation centers on setting up and controlling spray and roll-coating machines and on appearance judgment and is accountable for film quality. When choosing, it is better to first validate with one deliverable setup and test spray and inspection exercise rather than comparing names.

The basis for comparison is the task and work activity and work context descriptions on the O*NET-SOC 51-9124.00 page, the adjacent occupations and adjacent-occupation slug list registered in this evidence route, and the public occupational materials for each adjacent occupation; the comparison is an editorial compilation and does not constitute a conclusion about position authorization or mutual recognition of credentials.

The table below compares the positions and occupations adjacent to this one: architectural and maintenance painters, automotive body and glass repairers, painters (hand finishing), industrial machinery mechanics, maintenance workers, and fiberglass laminators and fabricators. The four columns answer the same set of questions: what this direction does, where the key difference from this occupation lies, and what kind of person is better suited to choose it.

Architectural and maintenance painters work on walls and components at building and structure sites with brushes or rollers; this occupation works at the machine and must control machine parameters and the beat such as viscosity and air pressure and gun travel speed.

People willing to work at building and renovation sites and accept height and outdoor conditions suit that direction; people willing to produce steadily on a spray line to parameters and beat suit this occupation.
Mainly on-site coating area and appearance and acceptance records.
Architectural and maintenance painters

Automotive body and glass repairers focus on body straightening and paint repair and glass replacement and usually deliver per vehicle; this occupation coats on machines per batch and beat, covering workpieces such as metal and plastic and paper and wood.
People willing to do single-vehicle repair and to work with straightening and sheet metal suit that direction; people willing to do batch coating and machine parameter control suit this occupation.
Mainly single-vehicle repair and paint delivery records.
Automotive body and glass repairers

Painters focus on hand brushing and rolling and decorative work, and their tools are brushes and rollers; this occupation works with spray and roll-coating machines and also carries equipment cleaning and parameter maintenance.
People willing to do hand finishing and craft effects suit that direction; people willing to fix process parameters and equipment condition into a repeatable process suit this occupation.
Mainly hand work and decorative effect delivery.
Painters (hand finishing)

Industrial machinery mechanics focus on equipment installation and commissioning and fault diagnosis and repair and do not apply coatings or judge appearance; the repair and maintenance in this occupation is limited to the duties and authorization of this position.
People willing to work on equipment structures and troubleshooting suit that direction; people willing to produce steadily around coating quality and adjust parameters suit this occupation.
Mainly equipment repair and commissioning records.
Industrial machinery mechanics

Maintenance workers focus on routine servicing and lubrication and adjustment and cleaning, and their responsibility is to keep equipment available; this occupation, beyond servicing, also carries coating operations and appearance judgment and waste disposal.
People willing to do routine servicing and equipment condition inspection suit that direction; people willing to manage both equipment condition and coating results suit this occupation.
Mainly servicing and inspection and work order records.
Maintenance workers

Fiberglass laminators and fabricators focus on mold layup and resin and cure forming, and their work object is composite parts; this occupation applies coating or paint by spraying or roll coating and controls film thickness and appearance.
People willing to do molds and composite forming suit that direction; people willing to do surface coating and appearance and film thickness control suit this occupation.
Mainly lamination and cure and part inspection records.

paragraphs: Boundary: the six risk cards below are summarized from the tasks and work context of this occupation to explain 'what you will encounter and how it can be controlled', and do not state incidence rates or accident probabilities; the applicable scope of each measure must be confirmed separately against the applicable jurisdiction and employer policies and equipment manuals.

Direct answer: the risks this occupation most needs to judge in advance come from four places: coating and viscosity and film thickness deviating from process and causing batch defects, hazardous energy not isolated and machine guarding failing and causing entanglement or shear injury, insufficient chemical contact control and ventilation and personal protection causing occupational health harm, and improper hazardous waste and waste solvent disposal causing environmental and compliance consequences; missed appearance defects and untraceable operating and quality records are also long-term problems.
O*NET supports the tasks and context, and U.S. OSHA and the Chinese Code and list each support their actual safety and waste rules, not a globally uniform shutdown or resumption permission.
Roles that carry out setup and coating operations

Insufficient parameter and first-article verification may cause batch sagging, orange peel, pinholes, and color difference and lead to rework and scrapping; the responsibility and cost must be checked against the actual rules and contract, and this round has no evidence supporting a uniform joint liability of company and individual.

Editorial quality check: check material and parameters against the approved process and the first article and anomaly records, with necessary stop and escalation per the actual safety procedure, and resumption and batch release confirmed by the actually authorized person.
Thickening the coating on feel to catch up with the beat; skipping first-article confirmation and starting the line directly.
Roles that carry out equipment cleaning and repair and maintenance

Internal repair, disassembly, and cleaning that actually falls under hazardous energy control, without isolation and verification per procedure, or bypassing guards to run hazards, may cause entanglement, shear, crush, or electric shock; not all cleaning is uniformly subject to LOTO.

U.S. OSHA1910.147 is limited to the repair and maintenance hazardous energy it covers; general production has its applicable conditions and exceptions, and not all setup and cleaning is judged to require LOTO. A person performing isolation must have the authorized employee duties and training under the employer's procedure, and ordinary operator status does not automatically authorize it; stored residual energy must be eliminated, disconnected, restrained, or made safe, with re-accumulation checked continuously where necessary, isolation and de-energization verified before work, and a stop button is not an isolating device. Re-energization follows the procedure for checking that equipment and personnel are clear and for notification, and is not decided by the operator simply because the anomaly has disappeared. U.S. 1910.212 requires the point of operation to be properly guarded against entry of body parts into the danger zone, and hand tools cannot substitute for guarding; guards must not be removed or bypassed without authorization to operate equipment in a hazardous condition, and repair and disassembly follow the actual control procedure, without treating any disassembly as per se unlawful.
Just pressing the button and reaching into the equipment; jamming the interlock with a tool so the machine keeps running.
Roles that carry out chemical use and ventilation and protection

Failure to identify contact with or inhalation of coating and solvent and cleaning agents, or failure to provide ventilation and respiratory protection per the hazard assessment, may cause acute irritation and long-term occupational health harm.

U.S. Hazcom checks labels and SDS and training against the chemical hazards; ventilation and PPE do not substitute for each other. U.S. 1910.132 requires the employer to assess hazards and select suitable and properly fitting PPE and provide training; 1910.134 prioritizes feasible engineering controls, requires a medical evaluation before respirator use, and requires fit testing for tight-fitting facepieces on first use and model or size change and at least annually. PPE does not replace ventilation, position authority, or judgment of safe dwell time. The 1910.107 ventilation provisions are limited to the applicable scenarios of spraying combustible or flammable materials.
Spraying continuously in an unventilated corner; mixing different coatings into unlabeled containers.
Roles that carry out waste and solvent disposal

Improper dumping of waste paint and solvents already identified as hazardous waste, or mixing them into non-hazardous storage, may cause pollution and liability; the category must be checked against the list or identification, and not all paint-containing material is automatically hazardous waste.

China's current Ecological Environment Code takes effect 2026-08-15; Articles 528–536 identify hazardous waste by list or identification, require identification marks, unit plans and ledgers and reporting, standardized storage, utilization, and disposal, classification by characteristics, and prohibit mixing incompatible materials without safe disposal; dumping or discarding without authorization or mixing into non-hazardous waste storage is prohibited, operating units must hold a permit, and entrusting unlicensed units or individuals is prohibited, with transfers following the manifest and cross-province approval rules. Article 1242 has repealed the old solid waste law, which is no longer used as the current basis. The 2025 hazardous waste list Articles 2/3/4/6 and HW12 identify by specific process and entry; the scope of 900-250/251/252/256/299 and similar entries differs, and some explicitly exclude water-based paint, which does not mean all water-based paint waste is automatically non-hazardous. Where the property is not clear, identification follows the standard, and not all paint-contaminated rags, drums, or water-based paint waste are judged hazardous waste across the board.

Dumping cleaning solvent without checking the category, or mixing paint-contaminated rags and drums already identified as hazardous waste into non-hazardous storage; the water-based paint exclusion conditions are checked item by item and cannot be treated as ordinary trash across the board.

A defect that is not identified or not determined may let a non-conforming batch reach downstream processes or the customer, causing rework and complaints and reputational loss.

Inspect and record per the inspection standard and sampling method; for defects whose determination is uncertain, escalate per procedure, and the release decision is made by the position with the corresponding duties.
Releasing after a single glance; treating a batch with obvious color difference as 'the customer will not notice'.

Missing records for the batch, coating, mix ratio, equipment parameters, or anomalies may hinder quality traceability and cause identification and proof of execution; this cannot be used to assert that the cause can never be located from other evidence.
Record operating data and anomalies and handover items on the prescribed forms, writing the time and batch and parameters clearly so that the records can be reviewed by others.

values: Fictional task: based on one fictional workpiece and coating system requirement and one set of fictional equipment parameters and inspection records, complete the setup and test spray points and the appearance defect investigation and handling plan.

Fictional material: a fictional production line and workpiece profile (including one instance of high coating viscosity and one instance of insufficient spray booth exhaust), fictional parameter records (including low air pressure and fast gun travel speed and film thickness above the upper limit), and fictional appearance inspection records (including sagging and orange peel and one color difference).
Fictional condition: a fictional equipment inspection and hazardous energy isolation and cleaning process (including stop and escalation thresholds).

Step one: write out the setup and test spray points (list the main parameters to verify and the first-article confirmation items, and point out the viscosity and air pressure and gun travel speed problems in the given material).
Step two: write out the appearance defect investigation and handling plan (explain the determination criteria and data sources and time, and which batches must not be released before verification).

Step three: write a one-page safety and chemical and waste handling statement (including hazardous energy isolation and ventilation and personal protection and hazardous waste classification points) and explain which matters require confirmation by an authorized position or a person with the appropriate qualifications before being carried out.
Reference deliverables: one setup and test spray points sheet, one appearance defect investigation and handling plan, and one safety and chemical and waste handling statement.

Evaluation basis: whether the parameter settings meet the process requirements, whether first-article confirmation is complete, whether the defect determination criteria and data sources are written out, whether hazardous energy and ventilation and protection risks are identified and escalated, and whether the hazardous waste classification meets the requirements.
Multiple reasonable framings are allowed; if you consider some information insufficient to judge, you should clearly write out which parts are insufficient and what additional information is needed.

The workpiece and parameters and process given in the prompt are all fictional values, used only to practice the setup and inspection logic and safety boundaries.

entries.answer: Daily work centers on machine setup and coating operations and appearance judgment and equipment cleaning and maintenance: starting and stopping equipment and attaching nozzles and adjusting spray dispersion, turning knobs and valves to regulate conveyor speed and machine temperature and air pressure and flow, spraying primer and topcoat at the specified amounts, applying rust-preventive primer and caulking and sealing seams, touching up repair areas with a brush, monitoring the operation and identifying and correcting defects, inspecting and measuring samples, disassembling and cleaning and reassembling sprayers, cleaning equipment and the work area, and disposing of hazardous waste per procedure and recording operating data. O*NET work context shows 87% use their hands continually, 79% are exposed to noise every day, 74% are exposed to contaminants every day, and 76% wear protective equipment every day.
entries.question: What do coating, painting, and spraying machine setters, operators, and tenders do every day?

entries.answer: Architectural and maintenance painters brush or roll at building and structure sites; automotive body and glass repairers focus on single-vehicle repair; painters focus on hand brushing and decorative craft; industrial machinery mechanics and maintenance workers focus on equipment repair and servicing; fiberglass laminators and fabricators focus on composite forming; platers and cleaning and metal pickling equipment operators and tenders focus on electrochemistry and chemical pretreatment; this occupation centers on setting up and controlling spray and roll-coating machines and on appearance judgment and is accountable for film quality. Shared capabilities do not mean the roles are interchangeable: the equipment type, coating system, and safety requirements differ.
entries.question: Where is the boundary between this occupation and adjacent occupations?

entries.answer: That cannot be inferred. The core tasks of this occupation include setting and confirming parameters, judging whether viscosity and film thickness meet standards, judging defect causes and whether to release, and hazardous energy isolation and chemical and waste handling; tool output neither replaces those judgments nor removes equipment and chemical safety obligations.
entries.question: Will AI replace coating, painting, and spraying machine setters, operators, and tenders?

entries.answer: The earlier-affected parts are those that can be structured and digitized: coating mix trial calculations, equipment inspection and parameter record organization, defect image archiving and statistics, and inspection and handover record drafts. The later-affected parts are those requiring judgment and accountability: viscosity and film thickness and appearance determination, defect cause judgment and rework or scrap decisions, equipment anomaly and shutdown handling, and hazardous energy isolation and chemical and waste handling.
entries.question: Which tasks are most easily automated?

entries.answer: Judging the workpiece condition and the actual equipment readings on site, deciding on shutdown and escalation, holding the safety and quality steps under high noise and time pressure, and handling chemicals and hazardous waste and protection boundaries. These capabilities depend on on-site training and accountability.
entries.question: Which capabilities are hard for AI to replace?

description.text: Coating, painting, and spraying machine setters, operators, and tenders set up and operate spraying and roll-coating machines to apply coatings or paint to products such as metal, plastic, and wood, centered on machine setup and operation control, coating work, and equipment cleaning and chemical disposal: the tasks and work context, the US wage and employment basis shown on the O*NET page (the exact 51-9124.00 basis is labeled), the mainland China statistical basis and position mapping gap, entry and qualification paths, and risks and one practice run, all in one view.

title.text: Coating, painting, and spraying machine setters, operators, and tenders

subject.name: Coating, painting, and spraying machine setters, operators, and tenders
subject.summary: Set up, operate, or tend spraying or roll-coating machines that apply coatings or paint using varnish, silver paste, copper, rubber, clear oil, glaze, enamel, oils, or rust-preventive materials to products such as glassware, fabric, ceramics, metal, plastic, paper, or wood, including transportation vehicle painters (such as painters in automotive body repair shops): start and stop equipment and adjust nozzles, flow, and air pressure, apply rust-preventive primer and do seam filling and sealing, monitor the operation and identify and correct appearance defects, inspect and measure or weigh or test samples, disassemble, clean, and reassemble sprayers or power equipment, and dispose of hazardous waste properly and record operating data on the required forms.
